text:
maria_ops: Quick heads-up — our billing report for Dedicated GPUs shows a region-shaped opportunity. eu-west1 H100 reservations are ~14% more expensive than our forecast vs us-west1 for the last 8 weeks. Can infra ops weigh placement tradeoffs?

devin_infra: Thanks. I pulled the raw billing export and compared committed vs on-demand. Short summary: H100 per-hour list differs by region and our reserved effective rate in eu-west1 is higher due to a combination of lower commit discount and interconnect fees. Link: https://go.redwood/sheets/regional-commitments (view only)

sam_eng: If we move more inference traffic to us-west1 for cost reasons, what's the latency penalty for EU users? Rough p50 numbers?

maria_ops: p50 EU->us-west1 is ~90-110ms for most regions, p95 up to 180ms. For many low-priority batch/async workloads that’s acceptable, but not for real-time chat SLOs. We should classify routes by latency sensitivity.

devin_infra: Raw numbers I posted to the sheet. Quick snippet from my calc: 
```
H100 list: eu-west1 = $5.28/hr, us-west1 = $4.92/hr
Commit 1yr eff: eu-west1 = $4.42/hr, us-west1 = $3.85/hr
Delta (effective) = $0.57/hr (~14.8%)
Egress delta = eu-west1 egress +0.6c/GB vs us-west1
```

lee_finance: Are those committed discounts locked or did procurement accept a supplier uplift in the EU region? Need to know if we can renegotiate or if vendor pass-through caused the higher effective rate.

cost-bot: [automated] Billing anomaly detected: committed discount mismatch in EU regions. Created ticket #BILL-7841.

devin_infra: I dug into the invoice lines — the higher effective rate is partly because we have a leftover short-term reserved pool in eu-west1 that wasn't auto-renewed; vendor billed on-demand for ~720h before the new commit kicked in. That explains the spike.

sam_eng: OK — operational question: can we failover EU chat traffic to a eu-central pool (cheaper SKU there) without code changes? Model artifacts, weights are replicated via the artifact registry. Need to confirm capacity and cold-start cost.

maria_ops: eu-central has spare A100 pool but not H100 at scale. For quality parity we'd need quantized variants (A100 + mixed precision) — needs evaluation. Also consider routing policy: latency-critical -> keep in eu-west1; background/high-throughput -> us-west1 or eu-central.

devin_infra: Proposal: short-term (30d) shift 20% of inference throughput for non-SLO traffic to us-west1 to capture immediate savings while we sort the eu-west1 reservation. Also open a procurement ticket to renegotiate the eu-west1 commit (lee_finance).

lee_finance: Sounds reasonable. I’ll open a vendor question and check T&Cs on commit termination/cancellation. If we can swap regions within the same commitment pool that’s ideal. Otherwise we do a new commit in us-west1 and scale down eu-west1 at renewal.

maria_ops: Action items: 1) devin update the sheet with hourly-sensitivity tags + run projected savings for 30/90/365 days, 2) sam run a small A/B latency/quality run for eu-central A100 vs eu-west1 H100 for the critical prompt set, 3) lee check vendor contract and escalate to procurement if needed. I’ll create a short RFC. :+1:

cost-bot: [automated] RFC draft created: https://go.redwood/rfcs/region-placement-2026 (maria_ops)

sam_eng: I’ll schedule the A/B for tomorrow morning and post results here. If we can keep quality within 2% and latency (<120ms p50), we can move non-critical inference.

devin_infra: Updated sheet with projected monthly delta and commit scenarios. Quick numbers for reviewers: monthly saving estimate if we shift 20% of non-SLO load -> ~$32k/mo. If we commit 1yr in us-west1 for that capacity, net saving ~ $18k/mo after amortized commit spend.

maria_ops: Great — thanks everyone. We’ll reconvene after sam posts A/B.
